args.message: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Problem
The nightly build fails: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Fix
- Import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money()`.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on this branch passed, including `tests/test_money.py`.
args.head: fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (FIN-212)

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Diagnosed the failure**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, while the test (`tests/test_money.py`) requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) per FIN-212 — e.g. `2.665` must round to `2.66`, not `2.67`.
- **Created branch** `fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212` and committed a one-line fix switching the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- **Ran CI** (run `ci-0001`) — it passed.
- **Opened PR #101** against `main` requesting review from **alex**: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The PR is now awaiting approval from alex (code owner) before it can be merged into main.

transcript.reasoning_content: Fix: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Check tests: 2.675 quantize with HALF_EVEN... Decimal("2.675") quantize to 0.01 with HALF_EVEN: the digit is exactly half; last kept digit is 7 (odd), so rounds to 2.68. Correct. 2.665: last digit 6 even, so rounds to 2.66. Correct.
